jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Backend
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About CodeRabbit

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

Role Overview

As a Software Engineer at CodeRabbit, you'll be contributing to the development of advanced applied AI systems that revolutionize code review processes. You'll work at the intersection of intelligent systems and software engineering, creating tools that empower developers to iterate rapidly in complex environments. Your expertise will be crucial in developing solutions that enhance code quality, scalability, and developer productivity.

You’ll help architect and build core backend systems — the infrastructure that powers our AI agent workflows, context-enriched code reviews, repo-level planning tools, and dashboard interfaces. You’ll work alongside AI researchers, infra specialists, frontend engineers, and product thinkers to build reliable, intelligent backend systems that power our developer tools at scale.

Responsibilities

  • Architect and build scalable backend services, APIs, and distributed systems

  • Collaborate with ML engineers to integrate models into agent-based systems and AI products involving autonomous or task-driven agents

  • Guide junior engineers through mentorship and technical reviews

  • Own architectural decisions in new product features

  • Ensure reliability, performance, and security across systems

  • Contribute to an engineering culture of speed, quality, and pragmatic innovation

Qualifications

  • Education: Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience

  • Experience: 5+ years building backend systems and distributed infrastructure

  • Technical Expertise: Fluency in TypeScript and Node.js, or a similar modern backend stack; experience with micro services, async job queues, and event-driven architectures

  • Systems Thinking: Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS/GCP), containerization (Docker/Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines, devops tooling, runtime infrastructure, and production observability

  • Engineering Craft: Strong understanding of software engineering best practices, including testing, code reviews, and version control workflows

  • Product Mindset: Thoughtful about trade-offs, user experience, and fast iteration

  • Team Leadership: Willing to mentor, lead by example, and influence technical direction without being a pure manager

Bonus Points

  • Experience with code search, code graphs, tree-sitter, or static analysis tools, and an understanding of how to apply them in real-world engineering environments

  • Experience integrating AI/LLM-based systems into product workflows

  • Contributions to open-source or community projects

  • Experience designing or implementing agent-based systems or AI products involving autonomous or task-driven agents

Why Join Our Engineering Culture?

  • CodeRabbit is building the next generation of AI-native developer tooling — starting with code review. We combine large language models with deep software engineering context to help teams ship faster, catch more bugs, and make better architectural decisions at scale.

  • We are a high-ownership engineering culture. That means no passive execution, no waiting for perfect tickets, and no narrowly defined task boundaries. Engineers here find problems before they're assigned, use AI as a core part of how they build, ship with judgment, and own outcomes from proposal to production.

  • Our operating philosophy: bias toward action, ship the smallest necessary coherent slice, validate proportional to risk, watch what happens, and make the system better. AI drafts; humans decide. Speed matters, but so does understanding what you ship.

  • This opportunity will be energizing for people who want real ownership, pace, and high standards. It's uncomfortable for people who prefer slow consensus or heavily managed workflows.

  • If you want to build tools that are changing how software gets written, and be held to the standard that the best engineers thrive under; we'd love to talk.

Our Values

  • 🤝 Collaborative Humans: Prioritizing collective intelligence

  • 🚀 Fearless Innovators: Turning obstacles into growth opportunities

  • 💪 Persistent, Passionate Developers: Thriving on complex, long-term challenges

  • 🎯 Impact-Driven Creators: Crafting intuitive tools for developers

  • 🧠 Rapid Learners and Un-learners: Adapting quickly in our fast-paced technological world

As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

About the Role

CodeRabbit is hiring its founding Platform Engineer. You'll own the compute, orchestration, and infrastructure layer that CodeRabbit's AI engine and every product on top of it run on, across a multi-region GCP footprint and a product suite that's still growing. This is a 0-to-1 role: you'll build the platform function from the ground up, set the technical direction, establish the patterns everyone else builds on, and make the early architectural calls that are expensive to unwind later. This role carries the same ownership and pace as the rest of CodeRabbit engineering, applied with the rigor that foundational infrastructure demands. The systems you build here need to be right, not just fast — everything else depends on them.

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years in Platform Engineering, Infrastructure Engineering, or Site Reliability Engineering with a strong bias toward building platforms, not just operating them

  • Deep, hands-on experience with Kubernetes: you've gone beyond running workloads to understanding and configuring the control plane, writing operators or controllers, tuning schedulers, and debugging at the runtime level; bonus if you've contributed to Kubernetes or built on its internals

  • Experience building and running large-scale distributed systems. You understand the trade-offs between consistency and availability, have debugged distributed failures in production, and have designed systems around them

  • Strong cloud compute background on GCP or AWS. You've built infrastructure, not just consumed managed services; you understand how compute, networking, and storage primitives work at the layer below the console

  • Proficiency in Docker and container runtime internals: image layering, networking modes, security contexts, and build optimization

Technical Skills

  • Container & Orchestration: CRDs, operators, admission webhooks, RBAC, network policies, autoscaling; strong Docker/OCI toolchain knowledge

  • Distributed Systems: queuing, eventual consistency, backpressure, graceful degradation

  • Infrastructure as Code: Advanced Terraform — module design, state management, programmatic provisioning patterns

  • Cloud Platforms: GCP (GKE, Cloud Run, VPC, IAM, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Load Balancing) — how these work under the hood, not just how to configure them

  • Programming: Node.js/TypeScript or Go for platform tooling, operators, and automation

  • Observability: Datadog, Prometheus/Grafana or equivalent — custom instrumentation, distributed tracing, SLO-based alerting

  • Systems: Linux internals, networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, load balancing, eBPF), storage systems

Why Join Our Engineering Culture?

  • CodeRabbit is building the next generation of AI-native developer tooling; starting with code review. We combine large language models with deep software engineering context to help teams ship faster, catch more bugs, and make better architectural decisions at scale.

  • We have a high-ownership engineering culture. That means no passive execution, no waiting for perfect tickets, and no narrowly defined task boundaries. Engineers here find problems before they're assigned, use AI as a core part of how they build, ship with judgment, and own outcomes from proposal to production.

  • Our operating philosophy: bias toward action, ship the smallest necessary coherent slice, validate proportional to risk, watch what happens, and make the system better. AI drafts; humans decide. Speed matters, but so does understanding what you ship.

  • This opportunity will be energizing for people who want real ownership, pace, and high standards. It's uncomfortable for people who prefer slow consensus or heavily managed workflows.

  • If you want to build tools that are changing how software gets written, and be held to the standard that the best engineers thrive under; we'd love to talk.

Our Values

🤝 Collaborative Humans: Prioritizing collective intelligence

🚀 Fearless Innovators: Turning obstacles into growth opportunities

💪 Persistent, Passionate Developers: Thriving on complex, long-term challenges

🎯 Impact-Driven Creators: Crafting intuitive tools for developers

🧠 Rapid Learners and Un-learners: Adapting quickly in our fast-paced technological world

What You'll Do

Own Technical Hiring End-to-End

  • Drive full-cycle recruiting across engineering, data science, ML, product, and technical operations.

  • Sit down with hiring managers and technical leads to pin down what "excellent" means for each role — the signals that never make it into a job spec.

  • Build interview loops that are sharp and repeatable, testing for genuine technical depth alongside the judgment it takes to succeed in a fast-moving startup.

  • Win candidates by making the scope, autonomy, and reach of what we're building impossible to ignore.

Source Where Others Don't Look

  • Hunt for engineers, data scientists, and technical PMs through advanced sourcing across GitHub, LinkedIn, and the technical communities where builders actually spend their time.

  • Construct pipelines for roles that demand both engineering rigor and the ability to thrive in a lean, high-velocity environment.

  • Reach talent long before they open a job tab — through open-source contributors, hackathon circles, and communities tied to developer tooling and AI.

  • Keep a working knowledge of movement in AI/ML, developer tools, and dev infrastructure so your outreach lands with engineers who can tell the difference.

Be a Strategic Partner to Technical Leaders

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to engineering and product leaders, giving them straight market feedback and real competitive intelligence on the talent landscape.

  • Give technical leaders the clarity to make fast, confident hiring calls — adding structure without the bureaucracy that usually comes with it.

  • Convert roadmap priorities into concrete hiring plans, and surface risks while they're still easy to fix.

  • Hold the line on speed, quality, and team fit as the company's technical direction keeps evolving.

Build a Recruiting Engine That Scales

  • Create and refine interview frameworks, assessment methods, and hiring rubrics that hold up as teams grow.

  • Bring consistency and standards to hiring without becoming a drag on the teams you support.

  • Lean on data, pattern recognition, and good judgment to keep raising the bar — and coach others to do the same.

  • Lay the groundwork for a recruiting function that can keep pace with where CodeRabbit is headed.

What You'll Bring

  • 5–8+ years of full-cycle technical recruiting, ideally at high-growth startups, developer-tools companies, or teams scaling engineering headcount quickly.

  • A proven history of landing senior engineers, data scientists, ML practitioners, and technical PMs in genuinely competitive markets.

  • Standout sourcing chops — real fluency with GitHub, LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean search, and the creative approaches that surface hard-to-find profiles.

  • Enough technical fluency to talk credibly with engineers about their work, read role-fit signals, and judge candidate quality well past the resume.

  • A high tolerance for ambiguity, shifting priorities, and leaders who think big and move quickly.

What You'll Own

Console, Settings & Configuration

  • Own the end-to-end product experience for organization-level settings, team management, and review configuration

  • Make complex configuration understandable and accessible for both technical admins and non-technical buyers, without dumbing it down

  • Work closely with engineering to define APIs, UI flows, and data models for configuration that scale across teams, repos, and deployment types

Access Control: RBAC & Custom Roles

  • Own the permission model end to end: define the roles, scopes, and capabilities that govern who can see and do what across settings, configuration, billing, and member management

  • Ship custom roles so admins can define their own permission sets rather than being boxed into our defaults, the table-stakes capability that unblocks larger, more security-conscious buyers

  • Get permission granularity and scoping right: org-level vs. team-level vs. repo-level access, and the inheritance and override behavior between them

  • Own audit logs and access trails, who changed what and when, as both an enterprise requirement and a pillar of our security and compliance posture

  • Treat least-privilege defaults, clear permission surfaces, and "no surprises" access behavior as core to the design, not afterthoughts

Billing & Subscription Management

  • Own the billing product: pricing display, plan management, seat-based licensing, upgrades and downgrades, and invoicing

  • Reduce friction in the purchase and upgrade path; design self-serve flows with correct proration, and partner with Growth and Sales on conversion and expansion

  • Own plan entitlements and feature gating, the mapping between what someone pays for and what they can actually use, kept consistent across the whole app

  • Handle the subscription lifecycle edge cases that quietly break trust: seat reconciliation and true-ups, renewals, failed payments and dunning, downgrades, and mid-cycle changes

  • Support enterprise purchasing: annual contracts, PO-based and offline billing, tax and invoicing requirements

  • Partner with Finance and Engineering on lifecycle correctness, and own the relationship with our billing infrastructure (Stripe, Chargebee, or similar)

Onboarding & Activation

  • Own the onboarding wizard and first-run experience for new organizations and individual users

  • Drive activation metrics: time-to-first-review, time-to-team-invite, and setup completion rates

  • Identify and eliminate the top drop-off points in the setup funnel

Who You Are

  • 5+ years of product management experience, ideally at a B2B SaaS or developer tools company

  • Technically fluent. You can read code, understand APIs, and have detailed conversations with engineers without a translator

  • Track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder product areas such as admin consoles, permissions/RBAC systems, or billing systems, where correctness and edge cases matter as much as the happy path

  • Strong instincts for simplifying complex configuration and access experiences without dumbing them down

  • Comfortable with ambiguity; can move from fuzzy problem to clear spec without hand-holding

  • You write well and communicate precisely. PRDs and tickets you've written are things you're proud of

  • Low ego, high ownership. You care about the outcome more than the credit

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience at a developer tooling, DevOps, or code intelligence company

  • Direct experience with RBAC, permissions, or identity/access systems, designing role models, scopes, and audit logging

  • Experience with billing infrastructure (Stripe, Chargebee, or similar) and subscription lifecycle mechanics

  • Familiarity with multi-tenant SaaS architectures, and with audit/compliance requirements (SOC 2 and similar)

  • Working knowledge of Git platforms (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, ADO) as a power user or PM

  • You've worked with or alongside a small, high-output engineering team and know how to match their pace

What This Isn't

We'll be upfront: this role isn't primarily about building AI features. If what excites you most is prompt engineering, model evaluation, or shipping AI-native UX, this probably isn't your best fit right now.

What it is: one of the most important, highest-leverage product bets we're making. The companies that win in developer tooling are the ones who nail the unglamorous stuff, setup, configuration, access control, billing, and trust. We need someone who genuinely believes that.

Who You'll Work With

You'll partner closely with our engineering leads (frontend, backend, SRE), the head of design, and with Finance, Growth, and Sales on the billing and activation surfaces. You'll report into Product leadership and work alongside a tight-knit, high-output India engineering team that moves fast and expects the same from product.


Our Values

 

  1. 🤝 Collaborative Humans: Prioritizing collective intelligence

  2. 🚀 Fearless Innovators: Turning obstacles into growth opportunities

  3. 💪 Persistent, Passionate Developers: Thriving on complex, long-term challenges

  4. 🎯 Impact-Driven Creators: Crafting intuitive tools for developers

  5. 🧠 Rapid Learners and Un-learners: Adapting quickly in our fast-paced technological world

 

What We Offer

 

  1. Work on cutting-edge technology with real-world impact

  2. Collaborative and innovative environment

  3. Competitive salary, equity, and benefits

  4. Professional development opportunities

 

To apply, submit your resume and relevant project samples or GitHub profiles. CodeRabbit is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion.

About CodeRabbit

About the role

Design at CodeRabbit sits at the intersection of craft, developer empathy, and deep technical complexity. As our Product Designer, you will shape how millions of developers experience AI-powered code review across IDEs, Git platforms, the CLI, and the web — surfaces with few established conventions, where the right interaction pattern hasn’t been invented yet.

Our work decides whether CodeRabbit feels like noise or like a trusted teammate: whether a developer trusts an AI-generated suggestion enough to merge it, or scrolls past it. We care deeply about the details that make an interface feel polished and trustworthy — the pixels, the motion, the copy, the edge cases — and we ship fast and learn in the open.

This is a high-ownership role for a designer who is exceptional at visual and interaction design. You will own design strategy and the design system across our product suite, set the bar for craft, and build a team of exceptional designers around you.

What you’ll do

  • Own end-to-end design. Drive the full process — from research and information architecture through high-fidelity visual design and sometimes implementation — for our AI code review platform.

  • Craft beautiful, trustworthy interfaces. Design polished, delightful UI that makes complex code analysis feel effortless and earns developers’ trust in AI-generated suggestions.

  • Set the interaction standard. Define interaction patterns, micro-interactions, and motion for emerging AI experiences — real-time review, conversational feedback, and agentic workflows — that feel native to how developers work.

  • Build and scale our design system. Create and maintain a comprehensive, scalable design system spanning Web, IDE extensions, Git platforms, and CLI surfaces.

  • Make complex data legible. Design clear visualizations and information architecture for code quality metrics, dependency graphs, and AI-generated insights.

  • Partner cross-functionally. Collaborate closely with engineering, product, and AI teams to define product vision, strategy, and roadmap, and to ship high-quality work in a fast-paced environment.

  • Stay close to the model. Design for where AI capabilities are heading, not just what they can do today, and prototype rapidly to communicate concepts and build excitement.

  • Raise the team’s craft. Establish design best practices, and elevate quality and consistency across broader product flows.

What we’re looking for

  • Exceptional visual and interaction design. You are highly proficient in both — a master of typography, layout, color, hierarchy, and motion, with an instinct for the interaction details that make a product feel alive and trustworthy. This is the core of the role.

  • You ship fast and elevate craft. You would rather get something in front of users this week than perfect it for a month, and you find ways to maintain care for the details while moving quickly.

  • You’re AI-native in how you work. You already use AI tools to extend what you can build and see AI as a creative partner in your own practice.

  • You’re rethinking the basics. Many UI primitives were designed for a different era; you’re excited to question assumptions and invent patterns native to AI and developer tools.

  • You lead through craft and collaboration. You communicate design decisions clearly, influence without authority, and lift the work of those around you.

You may be a good fit if you have

  • 2–5+ years of product design experience, with a strong portfolio showcasing polished UI craftsmanship and innovative interaction design.

  • A proven track record of shipping complex technical products end-to-end in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

  • Experience creating and maintaining scalable design systems across multiple platforms.

  • Mastery of modern design tools (e.g., Figma) and comfortable at prototyping with front-end code (HTML/CSS/JS) preferred.

  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills across cross-functional teams.

Nice to have

  • Experience at developer-focused companies (e.g., GitHub, Postman, Hasura).

  • A background in or strong understanding of software development and Git workflows.

  • Experience designing IDE extensions, AI/ML-powered interfaces, or motion design and micro-interactions.

  • Contributions to open-source design systems.

What we offer

  • The chance to define the design language for a category-defining AI product used by millions of developers.

  • A collaborative, high-velocity environment working alongside strong engineers and AI researchers.

  • Competitive salary, meaningful equity, and benefits.

  • Professional development and the resources to do the best work of your career.

Base pay range for this role is $220k-250k. Actual salary will be based on job-related skills, experience, and location.

  • Build and run a continuous experimentation program: hypotheses, instrumentation, A/B tests, and clear readouts on what won, what lost, and why.

  • Experience with developer tools, devtools PLG, or technical audiences.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About CodeRabbit

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

About the role

We're looking for a Design Engineer who lives at the intersection of design and code. You will prototype, build, and polish the experiences that make CodeRabbit feel like a trusted teammate rather than noise — across IDEs, Git platforms, the CLI, and the web, surfaces with few established conventions, where the right interaction pattern hasn't been invented yet.

Whether a developer trusts an AI-generated suggestion enough to merge it often comes down to execution: the pixels, the motion, the copy, the milliseconds of latency, the edge cases. This role owns that last mile. It is perfect for someone who thinks like a designer but builds like an engineer — or vice versa.

This is a high-ownership role working directly with design, engineering, and AI teams to define what's possible and then ship it, fast.

What you'll do

  • Build production-quality UI. Ship polished components and interactions that make complex code analysis feel effortless and earn developers' trust in AI-generated suggestions.

  • Prototype rapidly. Turn concepts for emerging AI experiences — real-time review, conversational feedback, agentic workflows — into working prototypes in hours, not days, to validate ideas before full implementation.

  • Bridge design and engineering. Translate high-fidelity designs into pixel-perfect code, and push design forward through technical innovation the mockups couldn't anticipate.

  • Own implementation quality. Set and hold the bar for UI execution across the product — smooth interactions, thoughtful motion, and micro-interactions that make the product feel alive.

  • Build the design system in code. Create and maintain reusable, well-engineered components spanning Web, IDE extensions, Git platforms, and CLI surfaces, so the whole team ships faster.

  • Make complex data legible. Implement clear, performant visualizations for code quality metrics, dependency graphs, and AI-generated insights.

  • Stay close to the model. Build for where AI capabilities are heading, not just what they can do today, and help define interaction paradigms native to AI and developer tools.

What we're looking for

  • Equally fluent in Figma and your editor. You move between design tools and code without friction, and you're credible in both rooms. This is the core of the role.

  • Strong front-end engineering. Deep skills in TypeScript, React, CSS, and animation, with an instinct for building reusable, maintainable UI systems.

  • An obsession with craft. You have an eye for design details, you've shipped polished products, and you know what it takes to get from 90% to 100%.

  • You ship fast and learn in the open. You'd rather get something in front of users this week than perfect it for a month — and you find ways to keep the care in the details while moving quickly.

  • You're AI-native in how you work. You already use AI tools to extend what you can build and see AI as a creative partner in your own practice.

  • You're rethinking the basics. Many UI primitives were designed for a different era; you're excited to question assumptions and invent patterns native to AI and developer tools.

You may be a good fit if you have

  • 2–5+ years of experience in design engineering, front-end, or product design roles, with a portfolio or shipped work demonstrating both engineering rigor and visual craft.

  • A proven track record of shipping complex technical products end-to-end in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

  • Experience building or contributing to design systems and component libraries across multiple platforms.

  • Strong command of modern front-end tooling (TypeScript, React, CSS, animation libraries) and modern design tools (e.g., Figma).

  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills across cross-functional teams.

Nice to have

  • Experience at developer-focused companies (e.g., GitHub, Postman, Hasura) or building developer tools.

  • A background in or strong understanding of software development and Git workflows.

  • Experience with IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains), Electron, or building cross-platform apps.

  • Experience designing or building AI/ML-powered interfaces, or motion design and micro-interactions.

  • Contributions to open-source projects or design systems.

What we offer

  • The chance to define the design language for a category-defining AI product used by millions of developers.

  • A collaborative, high-velocity environment working alongside strong engineers and AI researchers.

  • Competitive salary, meaningful equity, and benefits.

  • Professional development and the resources to do the best work of your career.

  • Turn detection-quality evidence (benchmarks, evaluations, real-world results) into product decisions and customer-facing proof

  • Partner with Sales on enterprise security evaluations and competitive positioning in the code security market

  • Shape pricing and packaging of the security offering with Growth and Finance

  • Work daily with the engineers building the agentic scanning pipeline; bring the customer and market view to detection priorities

🎯 Impact-Driven Creators: Crafting intuitive tools for developers

🧠 Rapid Learners and Un-learners: Adapting quickly in our fast-paced technological world

  • Collaborative and innovative environment

  • Competitive salary, equity, and benefits

  • Professional development opportunities

CodeRabbit's brand is how millions of developers first decide whether to trust us. As our Visual Designer, your home base is CodeRabbit's web presence — coderabbit.ai, product launches, and campaign moments — where you'll design pages, systems, and visuals that get built and shipped, not just handed off. But the impact is bigger than the site: you'll shape how the CodeRabbit brand shows up everywhere it lives, from launch announcements and event experiences to motion, illustration, and social, across digital and physical mediums.

Developers have finely tuned radars for the generic and the overhyped. Our work decides whether CodeRabbit reads as credible craft or as marketing noise — and we care deeply about the details that earn that credibility: the typography, the motion, the pixels, the restraint. We ship fast and learn in the open.

First and foremost, this is a visual design role. Exceptional creativity and design craft for the web are what matter most. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers who turn design into production code, and you're encouraged to get hands-on in the medium yourself — but we're hiring you for your eye and your ideas.

What you'll do

  • Define our visual language. Own the creative direction for CodeRabbit's most-seen surfaces — coderabbit.ai, product launches, and campaigns — and set a visual standard the whole company builds from.

  • Create the moments people remember. Design hero animations, launch visuals, event environments, and campaign work that lands with a developer audience across screen and physical space.

  • Own creative vision end to end. Carry work from the first spark of a concept to the finished result shipped on the real web, alongside engineers who turn your designs into production code.

  • Set the craft bar. Establish the typography, motion, and detail that make a page unmistakably CodeRabbit — the kind of work other teams measure themselves against.

  • Move fluidly across mediums. Work across web, motion, illustration, 3D, and brand identity, and raise the bar wherever CodeRabbit shows up.

  • Systematize the brand. Build visual systems and reusable patterns — not one-offs — so the brand scales consistently across every launch, page, and channel.

What we're looking for

  • Above all, a distinctive eye and original ideas. Exceptional visual design instincts and creativity are the heart of this role, and the web is where most of your work will live.

  • You ship fast and elevate craft. You would rather get something in front of the world this week than perfect it for a month, and you find ways to maintain care for the details while moving quickly.

  • You're AI-native in how you work. You already use AI tools to extend what you can build and see AI as a creative partner in your own practice.

  • You think in systems. You design components and patterns, not one-offs, and consider how each choice fits a broader visual system.

  • You know the web as a medium. You understand how layouts behave, what's buildable, and how design becomes code — and you thrive collaborating with engineers.

  • You make moments land. You've shaped launches, events, or campaign surfaces under real deadlines and know how to deliver when it counts.

You may be a good fit if you have

  • 5+ years of design experience with a portfolio spanning brand systems and multiple digital and physical mediums, anchored by strong, shipped web work.

  • Meaningful hands-on range across several of these: motion, 3D, illustration, environmental and event design, and interaction.

  • Experience designing for developer, B2B, or technical audiences, and comfort operating in a technology-driven environment.

  • Mastery of modern design tools (e.g., Figma) and an egoless, self-starting approach — you take feedback well and give it generously.

Nice to have

  • Ability to prototype or bring ideas to life in code (HTML/CSS/JS, React).

  • Experience contributing to a design system or brand system at scale.

  • Familiarity with CodeRabbit, Git workflows, or the developer tools landscape.

What we offer

  • The chance to define the visual identity of a category-defining AI product used by millions of developers.

  • A collaborative, high-velocity environment working alongside strong engineers and AI researchers.

  • Competitive salary, meaningful equity, and benefits.

  • Professional development and the resources to do the best work of your career.

About the role

Design at CodeRabbit sits at the intersection of craft, developer empathy, and deep technical complexity. As our Product Designer, you will shape how millions of developers experience AI-powered code review across IDEs, Git platforms, the CLI, and the web — surfaces with few established conventions, where the right interaction pattern hasn’t been invented yet.

Our work decides whether CodeRabbit feels like noise or like a trusted teammate: whether a developer trusts an AI-generated suggestion enough to merge it, or scrolls past it. We care deeply about the details that make an interface feel polished and trustworthy — the pixels, the motion, the copy, the edge cases — and we ship fast and learn in the open.

This is a high-ownership role for a designer who is exceptional at visual and interaction design. You will own design strategy and the design system across our product suite, set the bar for craft, and build a team of exceptional designers around you.

What you’ll do

  • Own end-to-end design. Drive the full process — from research and information architecture through high-fidelity visual design and sometimes implementation — for our AI code review platform.

  • Craft beautiful, trustworthy interfaces. Design polished, delightful UI that makes complex code analysis feel effortless and earns developers’ trust in AI-generated suggestions.

  • Set the interaction standard. Define interaction patterns, micro-interactions, and motion for emerging AI experiences — real-time review, conversational feedback, and agentic workflows — that feel native to how developers work.

  • Build and scale our design system. Create and maintain a comprehensive, scalable design system spanning Web, IDE extensions, Git platforms, and CLI surfaces.

  • Make complex data legible. Design clear visualizations and information architecture for code quality metrics, dependency graphs, and AI-generated insights.

  • Partner cross-functionally. Collaborate closely with engineering, product, and AI teams to define product vision, strategy, and roadmap, and to ship high-quality work in a fast-paced environment.

  • Stay close to the model. Design for where AI capabilities are heading, not just what they can do today, and prototype rapidly to communicate concepts and build excitement.

  • Raise the team’s craft. Establish design best practices, and elevate quality and consistency across broader product flows.

What we’re looking for

  • Exceptional visual and interaction design. You are highly proficient in both — a master of typography, layout, color, hierarchy, and motion, with an instinct for the interaction details that make a product feel alive and trustworthy. This is the core of the role.

  • You ship fast and elevate craft. You would rather get something in front of users this week than perfect it for a month, and you find ways to maintain care for the details while moving quickly.

  • You’re AI-native in how you work. You already use AI tools to extend what you can build and see AI as a creative partner in your own practice.

  • You’re rethinking the basics. Many UI primitives were designed for a different era; you’re excited to question assumptions and invent patterns native to AI and developer tools.

  • You lead through craft and collaboration. You communicate design decisions clearly, influence without authority, and lift the work of those around you.

You may be a good fit if you have

  • 2–5+ years of product design experience, with a strong portfolio showcasing polished UI craftsmanship and innovative interaction design.

  • A proven track record of shipping complex technical products end-to-end in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

  • Experience creating and maintaining scalable design systems across multiple platforms.

  • Mastery of modern design tools (e.g., Figma) and comfortable at prototyping with front-end code (HTML/CSS/JS) preferred.

  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills across cross-functional teams.

Nice to have

  • Experience at developer-focused companies (e.g., GitHub, Postman, Hasura).

  • A background in or strong understanding of software development and Git workflows.

  • Experience designing IDE extensions, AI/ML-powered interfaces, or motion design and micro-interactions.

  • Contributions to open-source design systems.

What we offer

  • The chance to define the design language for a category-defining AI product used by millions of developers.

  • A collaborative, high-velocity environment working alongside strong engineers and AI researchers.

  • Competitive salary, meaningful equity, and benefits.

  • Professional development and the resources to do the best work of your career.

About the role

Product at CodeRabbit sits at the intersection of developer empathy, frontier AI capabilities, and real commercial stakes. As a Product Manager, you will shape how millions of developers experience AI-powered code review across IDEs, Git platforms, the CLI, and the web — surfaces where the playbook hasn't been written yet and the models improve under your feet every quarter.

Our work decides whether CodeRabbit feels like noise or like a trusted teammate: whether a developer acts on a review comment, adopts an agentic workflow, or brings CodeRabbit to their whole organization. You will live close to both the customer and the model — talking to developers weekly, prototyping with AI tools yourself, and translating what's newly possible into products people rely on.

We are hiring across all levels, and we mean it. If you are early in your product career with sharp instincts and a bias for shipping, we will give you real ownership from week one. If you are a seasoned product leader or former founder who has taken products from zero to category-defining scale, we will give you problems worthy of that experience — and room to shape the product organization itself. We will calibrate scope, title, and compensation to you, not the other way around.

What you'll do

Depending on your experience, you will own a surface, a product line, or the roadmap itself. Across levels, the work looks like this:

  • Own problems end-to-end. Drive discovery, definition, and delivery — from customer conversations and data analysis through specs, launch, and iteration — for products developers use every day.

  • Stay close to the customer. Build relationships with the developers and engineering leaders who use CodeRabbit, run feedback loops with our largest customers, and turn what you hear into what we build.

  • Stay close to the model. Understand what frontier models can do today and where they're heading, and design products for the capabilities arriving next — not just the ones already here.

  • Prototype to learn. Use AI tools to build and validate ideas yourself before committing engineering resources. The cheapest way to answer a product question is often to build the answer.

  • Ship fast and measure honestly. Get work in front of users quickly, define what success looks like before launch, and let adoption and retention — not opinions — settle debates.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Enterprise Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About CodeRabbit

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

The Role

CodeRabbit is building AI-powered developer tools that help engineering teams ship better code faster. As a Senior Software Engineer on our Enterprise Engineering team, you’ll build the systems and features that make our platform reliable, secure, and scalable for large organizations.

You’ll own projects from design through production, working across backend services, enterprise integrations, and self-hosted deployments. This role combines hands-on engineering with customer problem-solving: understanding complex requirements, making thoughtful architectural decisions, and delivering solutions that fit into enterprise development workflows.

You’ll collaborate with engineers, AI researchers, infrastructure specialists, and product partners to bring intelligent code review to enterprise teams while meeting their needs for security, compliance, performance, and operational control.

What You’ll Do

  • Build enterprise capabilities. Design, develop, and maintain features that help large organizations adopt and scale CodeRabbit across their engineering teams.

  • Strengthen self-hosted deployments. Improve deployment, configuration, upgrades, and observability so customers can reliably operate CodeRabbit in their own environments.

  • Design for scale and reliability. Build backend services, APIs, and distributed systems that support demanding enterprise workloads.

  • Develop secure systems. Partner with the team to implement security controls and compliance-related capabilities that address enterprise requirements.

  • Connect enterprise workflows. Build and maintain integrations with customers’ existing developer tools and internal systems.

  • Work closely with customers. Translate customer needs into technical requirements, support successful deployments, and troubleshoot complex production issues.

  • Own delivery and quality. Drive projects through design, implementation, testing, release, and ongoing operation, following release practices that protect data integrity and system stability.

  • Raise the engineering bar. Contribute thoughtful design and code reviews, mentor other engineers, and improve team practices and tooling.

What You’ll Bring

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience building and operating backend systems or distributed infrastructure in production, ideally within SaaS or enterprise software.

  • Strong proficiency in TypeScript/Node.js, Go, Java, or a comparable modern backend stack.

  • Experience designing and maintaining APIs using REST, GraphQL, or similar approaches.

  • Experience with microservices, asynchronous job processing, and event-driven architectures.

  • Working knowledge of relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL, including schema design and query performance.

  • Experience with AWS or GCP, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and production observability.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals across testing, code reviews, version control, debugging, and maintainable system design.

  • Sound judgment when balancing security, reliability, performance, developer experience, and delivery speed.

  • Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate with customers and technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

  • A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus Points

  • Experience building self-hosted or customer-managed enterprise software.

  • Familiarity with enterprise identity, access controls, audit logging, or compliance requirements.

  • Experience integrating AI or LLM-based capabilities into production workflows.

  • Experience with code search, code graphs, tree-sitter, or static analysis tools.

  • Experience designing agent-based systems or products involving autonomous or task-driven agents.

  • Contributions to open-source projects or developer communities.

Why Join Our Engineering Team?

At CodeRabbit, engineers take ownership of problems and outcomes. You’ll help shape technical direction, work closely with the people using what you build, and carry your work from proposal to production.

We move quickly and expect thoughtful judgment. Our approach is to ship the smallest coherent solution, validate in proportion to risk, observe how it performs, and improve it. We use AI throughout our development process while remaining accountable for the quality and behavior of what we ship.

This role is a strong fit for engineers who enjoy autonomy, ambitious technical challenges, and high standards—and want to help shape how enterprise teams use AI in software development.

Our Values

  • Collaborative Humans: We prioritize collective intelligence and build together.

  • Fearless Innovators: We turn obstacles into opportunities to learn and improve.

  • Persistent, Passionate Developers: We stay committed through complex, long-term challenges.

  • Impact-Driven Creators: We build intuitive tools that solve meaningful problems for developers.

  • Rapid Learners and Un-learners: We adapt quickly and rethink assumptions as technology evolves.
